source.title: Lying Is Just a Phase: The Hidden Alignment Transition in Language Model Scaling

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper fits a power law to language-model validation losses as a function of parameter count, using the same loss-versus-scale measurement and fit form as the original scaling-law work.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own Pythia validation-loss power-law fit and its own benchmark-trajectory prediction results. Results about capability coupling, internal representations, steering, and frontier benchmark correlations are not rows here unless they bear on a listed claim version. The loss fit uses all eight Pythia models; it is not a small-run-to-large-run holdout test.
record.test_reason: The paper fits its own power law, L(N)=E+AN^-α, to Pythia validation loss (70M–12B). This bears on V1. It also predicts benchmark trajectories across scale with a sparse-regression ODE, including a held-out Llama-2 family, which bears on V6. Its main finding, that TruthfulQA falls while HellaSwag rises below a critical scale, also bears on V6. The loss result is a brief side analysis used as a contrast to the coupling result.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misses the central claim. The authors conclude that the coupling between reasoning and truthfulness flips from negative to positive at a family-dependent critical scale, which loss curves cannot reveal because Pythia loss follows a smooth power law. They say the critical scale can be shifted by width, data curation and architecture. A Pythia-derived ODE predicts held-out Llama-2 benchmark trajectories at 5.6% MAE.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a loss-versus-parameter-count power-law fit, but its main study concerns capability coupling; it does not test token or compute scaling, fixed-compute allocation, or loss extrapolation from small runs.

fits_no_version.finding: The sign of the local reasoning–truthfulness coupling flips at a family-dependent critical scale Nc (0.12B–7B), shifted by width, data curation and architecture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling laws for the interaction between capabilities, as distinct from individual capabilities, change regime at a family-dependent scale.

record.problems: The loss result is limited to one family and eight model sizes, and the paper reports no token-count or compute sweep. The loss fit covers the full reported Pythia range rather than evaluating extrapolation from small runs on held-out larger runs.

untested.parts: Token-count and compute scaling; ranges beyond 70M–12B; other model families.
No loss law is fitted on small runs and checked against held-out larger runs.
Width is studied only for capability coupling, not for loss at fixed parameter count.
No other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer scaling.
No prediction of downstream scores from pretraining loss; no benchmarks beyond the five listed, apart from frontier SWE-bench/GPQA correlations.
No comparison of fitting choices, parameter counting, schedules or data setups for loss exponents.

missing.what: Non-monotonic TruthfulQA scaling and the coupling sign flip: Pythia r(HS,TQA)=−0.989 below Nc; OLMo TQA unchanged at 31.1% from 1B to 7B while HS rises 13.9 pp; family Nc values in Table 1.
The ODE is predictive within a phase but fails across transitions: the OPT fixed-point fit breaks at the second compression, and Llama-2-70B is not modelled.

record.verdict_notes: This is a single-author preprint with strong claims. Benchmark scores are largely public or self-reported. The loss fit uses existing Pythia checkpoints, and the fitted constants (E, A, α) are not reported. R2 is an in-sample fit. The paper is inconsistent about the ODE's training data (Pythia alone vs Pythia plus Llama-1).

versions.untested_parts: Only parameter-count scaling is reported, for Pythia models from 70M to 12B. Token-count and compute scaling are not tested.
The paper does not fit the loss law on small runs and test predictions on much larger held-out runs.
No fixed-compute sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is tested.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count is reported for loss.
No other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer loss scaling is tested.
The reported prediction concerns benchmark trajectories across model scale; prediction from pretraining loss and performance on downstream tasks beyond the listed benchmarks are not tested.
The paper does not compare loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations across fitting methods, counting conventions, schedules, or data setups.

rows.subject: Pythia family (8 models; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss as L(N) = E + AN^−α across model sizes.
rows.measure: Power-law fit and constancy of N^α(L−E)
rows.value: R² = 0.9994; N^α(L−E) = 154 ± 2 across all 8 models; CV = 0.8%
rows.note: The reported aggregate covers the full eight-model size sweep; the paper does not report a held-out loss prediction from smaller runs.
rows.check: Parameter scaling only, on public Pythia checkpoints spanning about 2.2 orders of magnitude. Constancy of N^α(L−E) follows largely from the fit itself, so it is not an independent check. No baseline applies.

rows.subject: Pythia family (8 models; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Fit a sparse-regression ODE to benchmark trajectories across model scale.
rows.note: This is an aggregate error across five benchmark trajectories, not a separately reported result for each benchmark.
rows.check: This is an in-sample fit error: the ODE was discovered on these same 8 Pythia models. It shows the trajectories can be described, not that they can be predicted. It should be labelled as a fit, not a prediction.

rows.subject: Llama-2 (7B, 13B, 70B; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Cross-predict held-out benchmark trajectories using an ODE discovered from Pythia data.
rows.baseline: 10.2% MAE for the best polynomial baseline (degree 2)
rows.note: The paper reports one aggregate prediction error for the three held-out Llama-2 sizes.
rows.check: The paper is inconsistent about the training data. The text says the ODE came from Pythia alone, but the Fig. 2c caption says a TQA fit on Pythia plus Llama-1 predicts Llama-2. The paper also notes Llama-2-70B sits in a second transition the ODE does not model. The polynomial baseline is a comparison of methods, not a control for the effect.

relationships.condition: Pythia validation loss vs parameter count, 70M–12B
relationships.reason: A single power law fits with R²=0.9994 and shows no transition across the 8 models (R1).
relationships.display_finding: A single power law fits all eight models with R²=0.9994 and no transition.

relationships.condition: TruthfulQA below a family-dependent critical scale (Pythia, OPT, BLOOM, etc.)
relationships.reason: Based on the text, not rows: TruthfulQA falls as HellaSwag rises below Nc (Pythia r=−0.989) while loss stays smooth. The authors say identical-loss models can be in different phases, and the ODE fails across transitions.
relationships.display_finding: TruthfulQA declined as HellaSwag improved below the critical scale (Pythia r=−0.989), while loss remained smooth, identical-loss models occupied different phases and the differential-equation model failed across transitions.
